correctness.rationale: Within 0<b1<b2<1, 0<D1<D2 and 0<r<min(1,D1(1-b1)/(D2(1-b2))), differentiation yields sign(k')=sign(D1-D2+D1 D2(b2-b1)t). The exactly one positive rate-ratio minimum is nondegenerate. H=F1*k-F2 has H'=F1*k', starts at 0, is negative at the rate minimum and tends to positive infinity because k diverges while F1,F2 have positive finite limits. It therefore has exactly one positive zero after the rate minimum. G=F2/F1 obeys G'=f1 H/F1^2, so it has exactly one later nondegenerate minimum strictly below its endpoint levels 1 and rho_inf. This rigorously produces the five cases, the two strict thresholds and interlacing. The exact canonical rational witness reduces to a quartic with one positive root greater than 1 by Descartes' rule. Cumulative differences are negative near 0 and at infinity but positive at time 2. Local Taylor expansions yield square-root separation. Standalone verification of this package checked symbolic and 160 seeded parameter cases; finite tests are supplemental.

value.rationale: Separates two physically meaningful ranking observables, production rate and cumulative production, by exact distinct thresholds rather than a routine change of notation. Shows why a well initially and ultimately ranked inferior can become transiently superior in accumulated production even when both underlying well rates decline monotonically. Establishes five sharp regimes, strict chronological interlacing, nondegenerate onset and an exact algebraic witness. Quantitative classification may inform the interpretation of production comparisons, without implying empirical forecasts or commercial advice.
